messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT — Elevated 5xx and latency observed in eu-west-1 impacting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Alert rule: api.gateway.euw1.5xx_rate > 2% for 3m. Pager duty triggered.

sumi (oncall): I'm on it. Affected: Hosted endpoints and Dedicated GPU pools in eu-west-1. Confirming scope now.

maria (sre): I'm seeing a spike in 503/504s from upstream AWS API Gateway + STS calls in eu-west-1. TL;DR: control plane / auth calls to AWS in region timing out and causing retries upstream.

devon (infra): Logs from the ingress LB show connection resets to aws-managed endpoints. Sample: `curl -v https://sts.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` yields timeouts intermittently.

jenna (platform): Which customer-facing routes are the worst? Any embeddings jobs affected?

kai (dedicated-ops): Dedicated pools that rely on cross-region control plane heartbeats are seeing degraded health checks; two pools moved into limited mode.

sumi (oncall): Quick customer-impact estimate: Hosted: ~20% of eu-west-1 requests escalate to 5xx for a 5m window; Dedicated: 4 customer pools partially degraded. cc @alex for customer comms.

alex (customer-advocate): prepping a short note for impacted customers (internal). Will wait for statusbot update before sending externally.

maria (sre): Reproduced tracing: majority of errors have `x-aws-error-type: Throttling` and `x-amzn-requestid` present. Looks like AWS side throttling/backpressure rather than our runtime crashing.

devon (infra): Can we validate control-plane vs data-plane? Are model servers returning 200 but upstream auth failing?

maria (sre): Data-plane (model tokens) mostly fine when auth succeeds. The cascade is: STS/assume-role -> token fetch -> request -> if token fetch fails we 5xx.

sumi (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) enable short-term bypass for low-risk non-auth paths (where possible) 2) increase local token cache TTL where safe 3) route new user traffic to other regions (eu-central-1 fallback) 4) scale up retry-backoff to reduce pressure. Which is fastest?

kai (dedicated-ops): For Dedicated pools we can temporarily mark the ones affected as 'isolated' so new sessions are not routed there. Doing that now for pool euw1-ded-03.

jenna (platform): Sending a routing policy change to route traffic away from eu-west-1 for the hosted API: `redwood route set --region-preference eu-central-1,us-west-2 --scope hosted --temp 30m`

devon (infra): Confirmed command queued; should take 30-90s to propagate. Watch for spike in other regions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: routing config change accepted by control-plane (change-id: rchg-20241113-004).

maria (sre): We should also throttle internal bulk retryers. Adding a global jitter to retry loops now. Patch: `git apply <<'PATCH'\n*** Begin Patch\n*** Update RetryPolicy\n+  // add jitter and raise base backoff to 1s for 5xx from eu-west-1\n*** End Patch\nPATCH`

devon (infra): Patch merged to canary and will roll to eu-west-1 region nodes only. Canary rollout started.

sumi (oncall): Paging note: I'm going to request AWS support case and include our pcap/traces. @maria will you open ticket?

maria (sre): Opening AWS ticket now. Support case: 1234567890. Summary: `Intermittent throttling/timeouts on STS/APIGateway in eu-west-1 starting 2024-11-13T08:23Z causing elevated 5xx in our Hosted API`. Attached traces and sample request ids.

ops-bot: pagerduty-bot: Sumi acknowledged the page.

aws-support: Thanks for the report — we're investigating internal control plane saturation in eu-west-1. We'll update within 15m. (auto).

alex (customer-advocate): Draft for customers: "We're experiencing elevated errors in eu-west-1 due to an AWS regional issue affecting auth and control plane calls. We're routing traffic to eu-central-1 and mitigating retries. We'll update within 30 minutes." Approve? :thinking_face:

sumi (oncall): Send that and include link to status page. Mark severity P2 for now (customer impact but partial regional fallback in place).

statusbot: Status page updated: `incident: Elevated 5xx in eu-west-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated Pools — mitigation: routing to eu-central-1 in progress — next update in 30m`

devon (infra): Observability note: increase sampling on traces for eu-west-1 to 100% for next 15m: `otelctl set-sampling --region eu-west-1 --rate 1.0`

maria (sre): Can we bump local token TTL safely? We currently fetch tokens every 60s for certain flows. If we increase to 5m we'll reduce STS pressure but must ensure no privileges drift.

jenna (platform): For low-privilege service accounts we increased TTL to 5m temporarily. Config push done. List: `svc-low-embeddings, svc-logger`

kai (dedicated-ops): Dedicated pools: mark euw1-ded-02 and euw1-ded-03 limited. New sessions prevented. Old sessions kept alive to avoid immediate disruption.

ops-bot: system: autoscale policy for eu-west-1 bumped +10% for now (attempting to absorb rerouted load).

maria (sre): AWS replied: "We have identified an upstream routing flapping affecting STS endpoints in eu-west-1; mitigation in progress on our side." AWS suggests reducing token request rate as a mitigation.

sumi (oncall): Summary so far: routing away from eu-west-1, throttle/retry tune, token TTL increase for low-priv flows, isolate affected Dedicated pools, AWS investigation open. Next: monitor error rate for 15m window.

alex (customer-advocate): Sent customer note to impacted customers and support channels. No major escalations yet.

devon (infra): After routing change we see eu-west-1 5xx rate drop from 2.8% -> 1.1% within 4min. Latency tail still elevated for some requests that still hit eu-west-1.

maria (sre): Trace sample showing fallback: `x-redwood-region: eu-central-1 replaced eu-west-1` — good. Need to keep watch for capacity pressure in fallback region.

jenna (platform): Monitoring eu-central-1 token usage — it's within headroom but trending up. Will hold for now.

aws-support: Update: partial fix deployed on AWS side, STS error rate reduced by ~60% over last 10m. We'll keep monitoring and notify when fully resolved.

sumi (oncall): OK, looks like mitigation is working. Action items: 1) keep routing preference for 30m 2) keep token-ttl change for 60m 3) keep dedicated pool isolation until the control plane is green 4) update status page at 30m and when AWS confirms complete. Who's owning the 30m update?

maria (sre): I'll post the 30m follow-up and coordinate with AWS for final close.

devon (infra): I'll watch capacity in fallback regions and rollback routing if we see saturation.

ops-bot: incident-note: Handoff to evening oncall at 1738123800.

pagerduty-bot: Maria escalated a handoff to jenna (next-oncall) at 1738123800.

jenna (platform): I'll take the next shift and keep the incident open until AWS confirms fully recovered.

sumi (oncall): Handoff summary to jenna: routing away from eu-west-1, token TTL increased, dedicated pools isolated, AWS case 1234567890 open and reporting partial fix. Priority: P2.

jenna (platform): Acknowledged. I'll watch for customer escalations and coordinate rollback when AWS signals full recovery.

alex (customer-advocate): Noted. I'll follow up with customers post-close with a short incident blurb and estimated impact window.

statusbot: Status page update (follow-up): `mitigations active, error rate decreasing. Next update or closure on AWS confirmation.`

aws-support: Final update pending; we'll send when all STS endpoints are stable. (auto)

maria (sre): Logging final metrics snapshot before handoff: 5xx peak 2.9% -> now 0.9% after routing and TTL changes. Kept canary patch on for retry jitter.

jenna (platform): Thanks team. I'll keep the incident open for monitoring and post a postmortem template if AWS confirms root cause.

sumi (oncall): Closing active pager for me. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
